title: Witness the capture dim in another tool on an unlocked screen
goal: The screen darkening that a region capture puts up is supposed to show up in screen recordings and shared screens from the first instant, and the code that makes it do that has shipped. Nobody has actually seen it happen yet, because the Mac was locked when it was built and a locked Mac photographs as the lock screen. Watch it work once on a real screen, so the fix is witnessed rather than argued.
notes:
Blocked only on an unlocked screen. Everything else is ready: ONE command answers all four acceptance items now.

Run:
  ioreg -n Root -d1 -a | plutil -extract IOConsoleLocked raw -   # must print false
  Scripts/probe-app.sh --quit; open -a "$PWD/dist/Photonz Probe.app" --args --capture-diag
  cat /tmp/photonz-capture-diag.txt
Note the ABSOLUTE path: `open -a "dist/Photonz Probe.app"` fails to resolve.

Report lines map to the acceptance items in order: line 1 says unlocked; the "dim shows up in another tool's screenshot" line wants about 0.75 of clean; the "frozen picture under the overlay" line wants 1.00 of clean; the "window shadow below a test window" line wants the freeze path within 75% of the old path's depth.

The shadow line is still the real risk. The freeze moved from SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(in:) to SCContentFilter(display:excludingWindows:) with ignoreShadows = false, and the comment on ScreenCapturer.capture(screen:) records a 2026-07-03 measurement that the filter path synthesizes NO window shadows at all (filter path delta-0 luma under every window edge). ignoreShadows = false is supposed to have fixed that and it has never been checked. If the line says SHADOW LOST, the fallback is to keep the filter path only while the overlay is up and note it.

Geometry and mean luma already match the old path exactly (3456x2234, 0.4887 both ways on this run).

Also worth a real screenshot for queue/audits/2026-09-03-capture-dim-in-recordings.json, which ships without one and says why; /tmp/photonz-capture-diag-drag.png is written every run but is only worth shipping from an unlocked one.
acceptance: The probe report at /tmp/photonz-capture-diag.txt says the screen was unlocked on its first line
Its dim line says the dim shows up in another tool screenshot, at about 0.75 of clean rather than 0.99
The frozen picture under the overlay measures the same brightness as the real screen, so the world is never dimmed twice
A window drop shadow inside a captured region still looks the way it did before the freeze changed capture APIs

log.note: Screen was locked for the whole run (IOConsoleLocked true at start, middle and end), so nothing could be witnessed: a locked Mac photographs as the lock screen. Did the part that does not need an unlocked screen: --capture-diag can now answer acceptance items 3 and 4, which it could not have answered even unlocked. Item 3 (frozen picture brightness) was inferred from the live screen; it is now measured on the frozen picture itself via a new probe-only RectSelectionController.frozenImages. Item 4 (window shadow) had no instrumentation at all, and the earlier run could not get one because it compared two shots of an empty screen where a missing shadow and nothing to cast one look identical; the diag now puts its own grey backdrop plus white card on screen and reads the shadow band through both capture paths. Ran it on the locked screen to prove it works end to end: it correctly reported INCONCLUSIVE for the shadow rather than inventing a verdict. Blocked on somebody being logged in at the Mac.
